best_for: C# and .NET developers, and Unity, Unreal or Godot game developers, who want one IDE on Windows, Mac and Linux, and hobbyists who qualify for the free non-commercial license.
description:
Rider is the .NET IDE from JetBrains, the company behind IntelliJ IDEA and ReSharper. It is built on the IntelliJ platform and adds ReSharper's code analysis, navigation and refactoring on top.

You can open, build, run and debug desktop apps, web apps, libraries and services written in C#, F# or VB.NET, along with Razor, XAML, TypeScript and SQL. Rider flags problems with over 2,200 live inspections and offers more than 1,000 quick-fixes. It can decompile a third-party library to readable C# so you see how it works. Unit tests in NUnit, xUnit.net or MSTest run from the editor, Git, Subversion, Mercurial and Perforce are built in, and you can query and edit databases without leaving the IDE.

points.title: Free if nobody pays you for the work
points.text: Rider is free for non-commercial use: learning, hobby projects, open-source work without commercial gain and content creation. If you are paid for the work, even by a non-profit, you need a commercial license. A 30-day trial is offered.

points.title: The free license has strings
points.text: It needs a JetBrains Account, offline activation codes are not offered, and the IDE sends anonymous usage statistics that you cannot turn off. It renews each year only if you used it in the last six months.

points.title: Built with games in mind
points.text: Rider supports Unity, Unreal Engine and Godot with engine-aware analysis, navigation and debugging, and covers shaders, C++ and Blueprints.

points.title: AI is optional
points.text: You can connect agents such as Junie, Claude Agent, Codex or GitHub Copilot through JetBrains AI, a provider subscription or your own API key. Rider also works with no AI at all.

points.title: Hardware it expects
points.text: JetBrains asks for 8 GB of RAM with 3 GB free for the IDE, a 4-core x64 or Arm64 CPU and 10 GB of disk. Supported systems are Windows 10 and 11, macOS 26 and 27, and recent Ubuntu, Fedora and Debian releases.

points.title: Many versions on Windows and Mac
points.text: Windows installers come for x64 and Arm64, per-user or machine-wide, and the Windows listing goes back to 2021.2. macOS lists about 100 recent releases, from Homebrew and JetBrains' own release feed. Linux is not listed here; JetBrains offers a tarball, Snap or the Toolbox App.
